column.text: Bitcoin trades at $63,162, just above its 30-day swing low of $62,006, and that gap is the whole short-term story. Fear is at 10 on the Fear and Greed index, and total crypto cap is down 3.97% over 24 hours to $2.18T. The money flow is the problem. Wednesday's BTC spot ETF outflow was −$157.8M, a partial figure with issuers still reporting, and the seven-day net is −$1254.1M. ETH saw Wednesday's −$17.0M (also partial) and a seven-day net of −$268.8M. SOL was flat Wednesday at +$0.0M, with a seven-day net of −$9.7M. Net exchange outflows point to coins leaving venues while institutional money exits, which is a bearish combination. Positioning is the fuel for any break. BTC longs sit at 78.3% of positions, the long/short ratio is 3.602, and the crowd is still adding. The last 24 hours liquidated $53.2M of longs against $15.8M of shorts. Daily RSI is oversold across BTC, ETH, SOL, BNB and XRP, so a bounce is plausible, but the trend has not turned. Our regime is risk-off. Continuation shorts with momentum carry the tailwind. Longs need a real mechanism: deeply negative funding, a capitulation reading, a demand catalyst, or a failed breakdown at $62,006. "Looks oversold" is not a reason to buy. Dollar liquidity is flat, so price structure has to do the work. Watch the $62,006 line. A clean break opens a long-liquidation cascade. Until then, treat bounces as selling opportunities and make the bulls prove the reversal.
